case_title.quote: KILAKKATHA PARAMBATH SASI & ORS. v. STATE OF KERALA

number_of_accused.quote: The Trial Court acquitted all the seven accused.

accused_gender.reason: Gender of accused is not stated; names suggest males but 'Mixed' has no basis.

accused_occupation.reason: Occupation not stated; only BJP affiliation.

victim_gender.reason: Deceased Sathyan is male (brother of PW-1).

accused_victim_relationship.correct_value: Political rivals (BJP workers vs Congress workers); known to each other
accused_victim_relationship.quote: the accused belonged to the Bhartiya Janta Party whereas the deceased and PW-1 were workers of the Congress Party
accused_victim_relationship.reason: PW-1 recognised and named accused; they were political rivals, not strangers.

offence_category.quote: convicted under Section 302 r/w Section 34 IPC

statutory_provisions.correct_value: IPC ss.302 r/w 34 (conviction); charged under ss.147, 148, 307, 324, 302 r/w 149
statutory_provisions.quote: charged for offences punishable under Sections 147, 148, 307, 324 and 302 read with Section 149
statutory_provisions.reason: Conviction provisions right but charged sections omitted.

weapon.correct_value: Swords, axe, long knife (also crow bar and sticks alleged for other accused)
weapon.quote: Ashokan-accused who was armed with an axe ... Babu armed with a long knife
weapon.reason: Broadly right; omits crow bar and sticks alleged for others.

evidence_type.quote: The prosecution story is also fully supported by the evidence of PWs 2,3 and 4.
evidence_type.reason: Eyewitness and medical evidence were used.

aggravating_circumstances.correct_value: Political animosity; unlawful assembly; 58 injuries on deceased
aggravating_circumstances.quote: 58 injuries thereon, most of them incised and cutting wounds

trial_court_outcome.quote: The Trial Court acquitted all the seven accused.

high_court_outcome.quote: reversed the acquittal of four accused (the appellants)

imprisonment_type.quote: sentence of life imprisonment to the four appellants

neutral_facts.correct_value: Accused allegedly assaulted PW-1 and his brother at a bus stand with swords, axe and knife; PW-1 injured, brother died; charged under ss.147, 148, 307, 324, 302/149.
neutral_facts.quote: PW-1 was grievously injured while his brother died at the hospital.
neutral_facts.reason: Says 'the victim' later died, confusing PW-1 and brother; presents allegations as fact.

offence_severity.reason: Judgment gives no statutory minimum/maximum range.

attempt_completion.quote: his brother died at the hospital

physical_harm.quote: three incised wounds were found on him as well

number_of_offences.correct_value: Charged under ss.147, 148, 307, 324, 302/149; convicted of s.302/34 against four accused
number_of_offences.quote: convicted under Section 302 r/w Section 34 IPC

premeditation_planning.correct_value: Prosecution alleged accused waited at Babu's shop for the bus; Trial Court rejected it
premeditation_planning.quote: waited at the shop of the 4th accused Babu for the deceased to reach the place in the bus
premeditation_planning.reason: Planning was alleged by prosecution, so 'Not stated' is wrong.

motive.quote: the murder was the outcome of political rivalry

key_evidence_accepted.quote: The prosecution story is also fully supported by the evidence of PWs 2,3 and 4.

witness_credibility.correct_value: PW-1 injured and credible; PWs 3 and 4 independent; PW-2's presence accepted despite absence from FIR; PW-3 and PW-4 were named in FIR/accepted
witness_credibility.quote: Merely therefore because PW-1 does not refer to PW's presence in the FIR does not mean that he was not present.
witness_credibility.reason: Only PW-2 absent from FIR; PW-4 was named in FIR.

trial_duration.correct_value: Offence 24 March 1994; High Court judgment dated 23.05.2003; SC decided Feb 2011; trial judgment date not stated
trial_duration.quote: Judgment & Order dated 23.05.2003 of the High Court of Kerala
trial_duration.reason: Trial judgment date not 23.05.2003; that is the High Court date.

legal_representation.quote: U.R. Lalit, E.M.S. Anam, Fazlin Anam for the Appellants

investigation_status.correct_value: FIR registered; investigation completed and charges framed; trial concluded
investigation_status.quote: On the completion of the investigation, the accused were charged

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Trial Court alleged delay in FIR and flaws in investigation; Supreme Court found none
procedural_irregularity.quote: there appeared to be something remiss in the manner in which the investigation had been conducted
procedural_irregularity.reason: Alleged irregularities rejected, but 'None noted' omits them.

prosecution_argument.correct_value: Prosecution case: BJP accused assaulted Congress workers PW-1 and brother; State argued no FIR delay, PW-1 injured witness, independent witnesses.
prosecution_argument.quote: there was absolutely no delay in the lodging of the FIR
prosecution_argument.reason: Core story right; omits State's arguments before the Court.

defence_argument.correct_value: Defence argued FIR delay, discrepant eyewitnesses, no medical support, doubtful PWs 2-4, bus crew unexamined, no ground to interfere in acquittal appeal.
defence_argument.quote: there was an unexplained delay in the lodging of the FIR
defence_argument.reason: Vague; omits key arguments such as FIR delay.

legal_principle_applied.correct_value: High Court shouldn't interfere in acquittal appeal save exceptionally, but may re-appraise evidence and interfere if trial findings are perverse.
legal_principle_applied.quote: the High Court can re-appraise the evidence
legal_principle_applied.reason: Omits the High Court's power to re-appraise evidence.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Arulve/u and Anr. Vs. State represented by the Public Prosecutor

sentencing_rationale.reason: No sentencing rationale given; the description addresses conviction.
